extraction.name: BIG-Bench Hard (BBH)
extraction.description: A curated subset of 23 particularly challenging tasks from BIG-Bench for which prior language model evaluations did not outperform the average human-rater. These tasks require multi-step reasoning and include categories such as algorithmic reasoning, natural language understanding, and use of world knowledge.
extraction.creator: Mirac Suzgun, Nathan Scales, Nathanael Schärli, Sebastian Gehrmann, Yi Tay, Hyung Won Chung, Aakanksha Chowdhery, Quoc V. Le, Ed H. Chi, Denny Zhou, Jason Wei
extraction.rai:dataCollection: BIG-Bench Hard (BBH) is a curated subset of 23 challenging tasks from the BIG-Bench benchmark. Tasks were filtered based on specific criteria including minimum example counts, presence of human-rater baselines, evaluation metrics, and model performance relative to human baselines. The dataset uses existing BIG-Bench tasks rather than collecting new data.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data comes from BIG-Bench (Beyond the Imitation Game Benchmark), a collaborative benchmark with over 200 diverse text-based tasks including traditional NLP, mathematics, commonsense reasoning, and question-answering. Tasks were filtered to include only those with at least 103 examples, human-rater baselines, and multiple-choice or exact match evaluation metrics.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human raters were enlisted to manually solve each of the tasks and score them against golden labels to establish human-rater baselines. Human-raters were allocated a few hours per day to solve a sub-sampled evaluation set of a benchmark task, where they could use external resources such as the Internet.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The human-evaluation component took almost a year, during which the formatting and content of some tasks had been changed multiple times. The organizers acknowledge that one should be careful in interpreting these results because the scores are not fully representative of human performance. In some cases, the task description was hard to follow and could have been better-formulated.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Some tasks in the dataset require factual and general knowledge about the world as well as common practices and presuppositions in Western society, which may introduce cultural bias.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset shows limitations in tasks requiring world knowledge and cultural understanding. Some tasks show worse performance with certain prompting methods, and none of the language models perform better than average human-rater performance on certain tasks like Causal Judgement and Ruin Names.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for evaluating language models across multiple categories including algorithmic and multi-step arithmetic reasoning, natural language understanding, and use of world knowledge. Different model types (Codex, InstructGPT, PaLM) show varying performance across these use cases.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For all but three tasks in BBH, we take a random subset of 250 evaluation examples. For Causal Judgement, Penguins in a Table, and Snarks, we consider all the available test examples—namely, 187, 146, and 178, respectively—in addition to the three examples reserved for few-shot prompting.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: BIG-Bench was filtered using multiple criteria to create BIG-Bench Hard: (1) filtered out tasks with more than three subtasks, (2) filtered out tasks with fewer than 103 examples (3 for few-shot, 100 for evaluation), (3) filtered out tasks without human-rater baselines, (4) filtered out tasks that do not use multiple-choice or exact match as the evaluation metric, (5) filtered out tasks in which the best reported model beats average reported human-rater score, (6) filtered out extremely difficult tasks that are outside the scope of this work. These filtering criteria result in 78 clean multiple-choice or exact-match tasks, from which 23 tasks were selected as BIG-Bench Hard.
